name: Kotlin Trivia
description: An island near St Petersburg, the Elvis operator, null safety and coroutines — trivia about the language Android went "first" on.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: Which company created Kotlin?
cards.fact: JetBrains, maker of IntelliJ IDEA, wanted a more concise language for its own Java codebase.

cards.prompt: Kotlin is named after…
cards.fact: Much of the team worked in St Petersburg, and an island name nicely echoed Java.

cards.prompt: In which year was Kotlin first unveiled?
cards.fact: JetBrains announced Project Kotlin at the JVM Language Summit in July 2011.

cards.prompt: Kotlin 1.0 was released in…
cards.fact: Kotlin 1.0 came out in February 2016, after five years of development.

cards.prompt: In which year did Google announce official Kotlin support for Android?
cards.fact: Google announced it at Google I/O 2017, and two years later declared Android development "Kotlin-first".

cards.prompt: Android Studio is built on which IDE?
cards.fact: Android Studio replaced the Eclipse-based Android tools in 2014.

cards.prompt: Kotlin code can call, and be called by, code written in…
cards.fact: Seamless Java interop let teams adopt Kotlin one file at a time.

cards.prompt: What lets Kotlin code be shared between Android and iOS apps?
cards.fact: Kotlin can also compile to native code and to JavaScript.

cards.prompt: Gradle build files ending in .gradle.kts are written in…
cards.fact: The Kotlin DSL is now the default for new Gradle builds.

cards.prompt: Kotlin source files usually end in…
cards.fact: Kotlin scripts use .kts instead.

cards.prompt: In Kotlin, "val" declares…
cards.fact: Idiomatic Kotlin prefers val and uses var only when a value really must change.

cards.prompt: Which keyword declares a variable you can reassign?
cards.fact: Both val and var infer the type, so you rarely need to write it.

cards.prompt: Which keyword declares a function?
cards.fact: A one-expression function can even skip the braces: fun double(x: Int) = x * 2.

cards.prompt: What does the type String? mean?
cards.answer: A String that may be null
options: A type that is not known yet
cards.fact: Plain String can never hold null, so many null crashes are caught at compile time.

cards.prompt: What is the ?: operator called?
cards.fact: Turn your head sideways and ?: looks like Elvis Presley's quiff; it supplies a default when a value is null.

cards.prompt: What does ?. do, as in user?.name?
cards.answer: Accesses the property only if the value is not null
options: Asserts the value is not null
cards.fact: If user is null, user?.name is simply null instead of a crash.

cards.prompt: What does !! do in Kotlin?
cards.answer: Asserts the value is not null, throwing if it is
cards.fact: Kotlin fans call !! the "I know what I am doing" operator, and use it sparingly.

cards.prompt: Which kind of class gets equals, hashCode, toString and copy generated for free?
cards.fact: A one-line data class replaces dozens of lines of Java boilerplate.

cards.prompt: By default, Kotlin classes are…
cards.answer: final, so they cannot be subclassed
cards.fact: Mark a class open to allow inheritance, the opposite of Java's default.

cards.prompt: Which Kotlin expression replaces Java's switch?
cards.fact: when can match values, ranges and types, and it returns a value.

cards.prompt: Inside a one-parameter lambda, what is the parameter called by default?
cards.fact: That is why list.map { it * 2 } works without naming anything.

cards.prompt: What is Kotlin's equivalent of Java's void?
cards.fact: Unit is a real type with exactly one value, also called Unit.

cards.prompt: What does Kotlin use for lightweight asynchronous code?
cards.fact: Coroutines let async code read top to bottom, like ordinary code.

cards.prompt: Which keyword marks a function that can pause without blocking a thread?
cards.fact: A suspend function can only be called from a coroutine or another suspend function.

cards.prompt: In Kotlin, semicolons at the end of lines are…
cards.fact: You only need one to put two statements on the same line.

cards.prompt: What is "Hello, $name" an example of?
cards.fact: Use ${...} with braces for longer expressions, like ${user.name}.

cards.prompt: What does 1..5 represent?
cards.fact: Use 1 until 5 to leave out the upper end.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: Dividing two Ints gives an Int; write 10.0 / 4 to get 2.5.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: length is a property in Kotlin, so it has no parentheses.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: repeat builds a new String; the original is unchanged.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: map transforms every element and returns a new list.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: The Elvis operator returns the right side when the left side is null.

cards.prompt: What does this print?
cards.fact: 1..4 includes both ends, so this is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
